author: product-requirements-expert
title: Vet list can be narrowed to the holders of one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian-directory surfaces accept an optional specialty value that narrows the list to the veterinarians holding that specialty. Matching is on the whole name and ignores letter case. The same slice locks the machine-readable list as a supported surface (REQ-VET-003).
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-004] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty; paging counts the narrowed list.
[REQ-VET-004] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty.
[REQ-VET-004] The match is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case on both surfaces; a leading fragment of a name (for example 'radio' for 'radiology') matches no veterinarian.

[REQ-VET-004] A specialty no veterinarian holds returns HTTP 200 with an empty veterinarian list on both surfaces: the normal page renders, and the JSON document carries an empty list. No error page, no 404.
[REQ-VET-004] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as an absent parameter on both surfaces, mirroring the empty owner search.
[REQ-VET-004] Without the parameter, both surfaces behave as they do today, including page size and paging.
[REQ-VET-004] Pagination links on the HTML page carry the specialty value, so following a link keeps the list narrowed to the same specialty.
[REQ-VET-004] Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter; the HTML page markup adds no such control.
[REQ-VET-004] A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed when any one of those specialties is named.
[REQ-VET-003] The JSON list at /vets is covered by a test asserting it carries the same veterinarians and specialties the HTML page shows.
non_goals: A visible specialty control on either surface — no form, dropdown, or link set. A control is a possible follow-up request.
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits: NG-9 is narrowed, not withdrawn.
Combining more than one specialty in one request.
Any write path over veterinarians or specialties (NG-2).
New user-facing wording, and therefore no message-bundle change across the eleven languages (REQ-LANG-002).
notes: URL contract, kept out of the PRD prose as mechanism: /vets.html?specialty=<name> and /vets?specialty=<name>; the parameter name is 'specialty'. Owner decisions recorded 2026-08-23 in docs/adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md (NG-9 narrowed; JSON surface reinstated as REQ-VET-003; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused). Two items for system-design-expert, outside product-requirements-expert write scope: add the 2026-08-23 non-goal ADR row to docs/adr/README.md index, and update the Contracts table Implements column for VetController and VetRepository with REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004. Three open questions are recorded in the PRD rather than blocking: visible control, empty-result wording, repeated specialty values.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing lands entirely inside the existing vet feature package and the existing controller-to-repository shape; no new package, type, or layer. What is new is the decision recorded in ADR 2026-08-23-specialty-narrowing-as-a-case-folded-query: the filter is a derived Spring Data read on VetRepository with case folding expressed in the query (IgnoreCase), not an in-memory filter over the cached whole list and not plain equality leaning on the column collation. Collation-dependence is the construction that produced the PostgreSQL owner-search defect (system-design.md#known-defects); folding in the query keeps the narrowing identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. Because the narrowing sits in the query, Page counts the narrowed list for free. REQ-VET-003 needs no code: reinstating the machine-readable list is a documentation and test-coverage act, and the stale Known Defects row calling that route pending removal has been deleted.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two narrowing reads over the existing Vet-to-Specialty many-to-many: a paged one for the page and a whole one for the machine-readable list. Derive them from the method name over the specialties.name path with IgnoreCase and Distinct, and carry the same @Transactional(readOnly = true) the existing reads carry. If name derivation is ambiguous, disambiguate the property path with an underscore before reaching for an explicit query.
Neither narrowing read is annotated @Cacheable. The vets cache has no eviction and these reads are keyed by caller text; the unnarrowed reads keep their caching untouched.

VetController normalizes the requested value once (absent, empty, or whitespace-only all collapse to no narrowing) and both handlers share that one normalization and the read it selects, so the two surfaces cannot answer differently. Put the normalization in one private helper, not once per handler.

The unnarrowed path stays literally vetRepository.findAll / findAll(pageable). Do not route it through the narrowing query: the join over specialties drops veterinarians holding no specialty, which REQ-VET-001 requires the page to list.

vetList.html paging links carry the narrowing value. Add it to the model as the normalized value and build the links with the Thymeleaf URL-parameter syntax, for example @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}.

patterns.description: derived paged query with a Pageable second argument: the shape the narrowing reads follow

the empty-search normalization the acceptance criteria point at: null becomes empty, otherwise strip. The vet filter reuses the normalization but not the fallthrough, because equality on an empty name matches nothing where startingWith on an empty name matches everything, so a blank value must select the unnarrowed read
the existing pagination helper: page size is a local, one-based page arrives as a request parameter, PageRequest is zero-based
real-repository vet test against the seeded data (radiology, surgery, dentistry; Douglas holds two): the home for the case-folding and whole-name assertions

risks.risk: VetControllerTests stubs VetRepository with @MockitoBean, so every controller test passes whatever the stub returns. Case-insensitivity, whole-name-not-prefix, and the narrowed page count are properties of the derived query, and a stubbed test asserts none of them while appearing to cover them.
risks.mitigation: Assert those three at the repository against the real seeded data in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest). Keep the controller tests for what they can actually see: parameter binding, the blank-value fallthrough, the model attributes, and that the two surfaces call the same read.

risks.risk: The narrowing value is caller-controlled text that reaches an href. The current paging links interpolate with the __${...}__ preprocessing form, which concatenates rather than encodes; copying that form for a string parameter would put unencoded caller text into a link.
risks.mitigation: Use the Thymeleaf URL-parameter syntax so the value is URL-encoded. Never concatenate it into the link expression. The value is not rendered as page text anywhere, and this slice adds no wording.

risks.risk: A distinct count query paired with a join has historically been the fragile part of derived paged queries; a wrong count would report page numbers over the whole directory instead of the narrowed list.
risks.mitigation: The paging test must span more than one page of narrowed results and assert totalPages and totalItems over the narrowed list, not just that the second page still filters.

risks.risk: An inner join in the narrowing read silently excludes veterinarians holding no specialty. Correct for a narrowed request, wrong if the same query ever serves the unnarrowed path.
risks.mitigation: Keep the two paths on separate repository methods, as the ADR records. A later refactor merging them needs a left join and a null-tolerant predicate.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because the case-folding location and the cache scope are decisions with rejected alternatives, not an adjustment; ADR docs/adr/2026-08-23-specialty-narrowing-as-a-case-folded-query.md records them. || Both items flagged by product-requirements-expert are done: docs/adr/README.md now indexes the 2026-08-23 non-goal ADR (and the new one), and docs/system-design.md#contracts now maps VetController to REQ-VET-001/003/004 and VetRepository to REQ-VET-001/004. || Two further system-design.md corrections the reinstatement forced, beyond the flagged items: the Vets row moved from an em dash to REQ-VET-003 (it was an unlisted fourth kind under a note naming only three, and it is now the document root of a supported surface), and the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route pending removal was deleted as false, with the provenance line's confirmed-defect count corrected from four to three. A short paragraph in the Persistence section records that this narrowing folds case in the query while pet-name uniqueness and owner search leave it to the schema. || Observation, out of scope: owners/ownersList.html paging links do not carry the last-name search, so paging an owner search silently widens it. REQ-VET-004 requires the opposite on the vet page, so the vet template must not copy the owner template here. Whether the owner side is a defect is a product question this slice does not raise. || The three PRD open questions (visible control, empty-result wording, repeated specialty values) need no design position: each is answered by doing nothing beyond the acceptance criteria. A repeated parameter binds to the first value under Spring MVC String binding, which is the narrowest reading and needs no code to enforce. || Open question recorded rather than blocked on: if the template renders an absent narrowing as an empty parameter, the paging links carry a valueless specialty parameter. Behavior is unaffected because a blank value narrows nothing, but the unnarrowed page's markup then differs from today's. Prefer omitting the parameter when absent; accept the empty form if omitting costs a template branch.

approved_aspects: VetRepository derived queries use Distinct + IgnoreCase over specialties.name exactly per the ADR, with @Transactional(readOnly = true) and deliberately no @Cacheable, each documented with a javadoc explaining why (separate from findAll, not cached)
VetController's narrowingSpecialty helper is the single normalization point shared by showVetList and showResourcesVetList, so the two surfaces cannot diverge on blank/absent handling
The unnarrowed path in both findPaginated and findVets stays literally on vetRepository.findAll(...), preserving vets holding no specialty and today's caching

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: both narrowing reads are Spring Data derived queries (findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, with and without Pageable) declared on VetRepository. The method name is parsed against the JPA metamodel at bootstrap and the caller value binds as a query parameter; no query text is concatenated anywhere in the diff. Swept src/main for @Query and string-built JPQL/SQL in the change surface - none.

Reflected XSS on the HTML surface: the caller-controlled specialty reaches vetList.html only as a URL-parameter value inside th:href link expressions. Thymeleaf URL-encodes query-parameter values in the @{path(name=value)} form and HTML-escapes the attribute, so a payload such as "><script> cannot break out of the href or the tag. specialty is never rendered as element text or into an unescaped construct; grep of the template confirms no th:utext, no inlined javascript block, and no DOM injection point.

Paging-link sweep is exhaustive: all five link sites in vetList.html (numbered pages, first, previous, next, last) were converted from the @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} preprocessing-concatenation form to the @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})} URL-parameter form, and all five carry the specialty. No concatenated-URL site remains in the changed template. Remaining __${...}__ sites elsewhere (owners templates, layout fragment, field fragments) are outside the change surface and carry numeric ids, not request-derived text.

JSON surface exposes nothing the page does not: /vets and /vets.html both pre-existed; this change adds only a @RequestParam to each. The narrowed read returns the same Vet entity graph as the pre-existing findAll(), so the serialized document carries the same fields (name, specialties) over a strict subset of the same rows. No new endpoint, no broadened management exposure, no echo of the caller's specialty into the JSON document - the 'widening the exposed surface' row of docs/security-principles.md is not triggered.

Input handling at the boundary: narrowingSpecialty is a single shared normalization applied identically on both handlers, mapping absent, empty, and whitespace-only to null so a blank value degrades to the unnarrowed list rather than to an unconstrained query. specialty binds as a scalar @RequestParam, not into a command object, so no new mass-assignment or identifier-binding surface is introduced.
Cache safety: the new reads are deliberately not @Cacheable, documented in the repository javadoc, so caller-supplied text cannot key entries into the eviction-less 'vets' cache.
No secrets: sweep of the full diff for password/secret/token/apikey/credential returned no hits; no new credential, connection string, or configuration value is introduced.

Supply chain unchanged: the change set touches no build file - build.gradle, the version catalog, and the declared repositories are untouched, so no new dependency, no version change, and no plain-HTTP resolution path. Framework baseline (Spring Boot 4.1.0, Java 25) is unmodified by this slice.
